import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 11
    n_vehicles = 6
    Q = 50  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[26, 13], [36, 75], [8, 40], [87, 28], [58, 94], [34, 25], [55, 18], [7, 66], [86, 64], [13, 80], [95, 31]]
    demands = [6, 24, 8, 25, 10, 5, 11, 7, 7, 16, 7]
    time_windows = [[0, 325], [57, 109], [42, 95], [43, 128], [53, 124], [65, 122], [33, 97], [57, 147], [40, 119], [51, 149], [67, 139], [67, 164]]
    service_times = [11, 11, 7, 6, 11, 8, 8, 13, 10, 12, 11]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Route Planning and Field Operations
From: Logistics Operations Manager
Subject: Routing and Scheduling Requirements for the Upcoming Delivery Horizon
Date: [Today]

Purpose
We will execute a single-day delivery operation from our central depot using a fleet of identical vehicles. This memo outlines the routing and scheduling requirements to ensure every customer is served on time while controlling distance-driven and fleet deployment costs.

Operational Challenge
- All deployed vehicles will depart the depot at time 0, each completing one continuous trip: leave the depot, visit an assigned sequence of customers, and return to the depot before the end of the planning horizon (the depot’s latest time).
- Every customer must be visited exactly once, with the start of service falling within that customer’s acceptable delivery window.
- We must determine how many vehicles to deploy (up to the available fleet), which customers each vehicle will serve, and the sequence and timing of those stops, while ensuring all constraints are satisfied.

Operating Rules and Constraints
- Fleet and trips:
  - Vehicles are identical in capacity and operating profile.
  - Each vehicle, if used, departs at time 0 and must return to the depot before the depot’s latest time.
  - Each vehicle may make only one trip; no mid-shift returns to reload or secondary tours.
- Customer time windows:
  - Each customer has an earliest and latest acceptable start-of-service time. Service must begin within this window.
  - If a vehicle arrives before the window opens, it must wait on site until service can begin.
- Service times:
  - Each customer requires a specific unloading/service time.
  - The vehicle’s departure from a customer occurs at the later of its arrival time or the window opening time, plus the required service time.
- Capacity:
  - Each customer has a delivery demand.
  - The total demand assigned to any vehicle may not exceed its carrying capacity at any point on its route.
  - No split deliveries, transfers between vehicles, or mid-route replenishment are allowed.
- Travel times and distances:
  - Travel time between any two locations is taken as the straight-line distance between their coordinates, using a consistent unit system where one unit of distance equals one unit of time.
- Depot time horizon:
  - All routes must be scheduled so that vehicles return before the depot’s latest time, ensuring completion within the planning horizon.

Cost Structure and Goal
- Using a vehicle incurs a fixed deployment cost in addition to the distance-based travel cost.
- The goal is to assign customers to routes and sequence stops to minimize the combined total of travel distance and vehicle deployment costs while meeting all time window, service, capacity, and return-to-depot constraints.

Expected Planning Outputs
- A set of routes (one per deployed vehicle) that lists the sequence of customers, planned arrival times, any waiting time, service start and end times, and the return time to the depot.
- Confirmation that each customer is visited exactly once within their time window.
- Load profiles per route demonstrating that vehicle capacity is never exceeded.
- A summary of deployed vehicles versus those left idle to balance service quality and total cost.

Assumptions and Exclusions
- Distances are symmetric and based solely on map coordinates; traffic, road restrictions, and parking constraints are not modeled.
- Vehicles are identical, and all parameters required for planning are provided in the data annex below.
